'''Yahya El Mashad''' ({{langx|ar|يحيى المشد}}; 1932 – 14 June 1980) was an Egyptian nuclear scientist who headed the [[Iraq and weapons of mass destruction|Iraqi nuclear program]]. He was killed in a [[Paris]] hotel room in June 1980, in an operation generally attributed to the [[Mossad]].<ref name=berfman>{{cite news|last=Bergman|first=Ronen|title=Killing the Killers|url= http://www.newsweek.com/2010/12/13/killing-the-killers.html|newspaper=Newsweek|date=13 December 2010}}</ref><ref name= hider>{{cite news|last=Hider|first=James|title=The secret life of Tzipi Livni|url= http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/middle_east/article4791158.ece|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101118021048/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/middle_east/article4791158.ece|url-status= dead|archive-date= 18 November 2010|newspaper=The Times|date=20 September 2008|location= London}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,950533-4,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110318165849/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,950533-4,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 March 2011|magazine=Time|title=Attack – and Fallout: Israel and Iraq|date=22 June 1981}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
El Mashad was born in [[Benha]], [[Egypt]] in 1932.<ref name=sisgov>{{cite web|title=ﻡ؟ﺵﻡ؟ﺵﻡ؟ﺵﻡ؟ﺵ ﻡ؟ﺵﻡ؟ﺵﻡ؟ﺵﻡ؟ﺵﻡ؟ﺵ|url=http://www.sis.gov.eg/VR/figures/arabic/html/17d.htm|website=Egyptian Figures|location=Egypt|publisher=State Information Service|access-date=24 August 2011|language=ar|archive-date=1 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111001185522/http://www.sis.gov.eg/VR/figures/arabic/html/17d.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was educated in [[Tanta]] and graduated from the Electrical Engineering Department in the Faculty of Engineering at [[Alexandria University]] in 1952.<ref name=sisgov/> Although he traveled to [[London]] to gain his doctorate in 1956, due to the [[Suez Crisis]] he eventually traveled to [[Moscow]] to complete his studies.  He spent about six years in the [[Soviet Union]] before returning to Egypt in 1964 to accept a professorship in [[nuclear engineering]] at [[Alexandria University]].<ref name=sisgov />

==Career==
El Mashad joined the [[Egyptian Atomic Energy Authority]] and worked as a nuclear engineer until the [[Nuclear energy in Egypt|Egyptian nuclear program]] was frozen following the [[Six-Day War]] in 1967.<ref name = sisgov /> He then travelled to [[Iraq]] where he led the Iraqi nuclear program,<ref>{{Cite book|title=The uncertain alliance: the US and Israel from Kennedy to the peace process|last=Druks|first= Herbert|page=225|year=2001|publisher=[[Greenwood Publishing Group]]|isbn=978-0-313-31424-7}}</ref> and supervised Iraq's nuclear co-operation agreement with [[France]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Can the Arabs win the nuclear race with Israel?|last=Perera|first=Judith |page=32|year=1983|publisher=Arab Research Centre|isbn=978-0-907233-13-8}}</ref> In 1980, he refused to receive a uranium shipment as it did not meet the agreed specifications, after which the French insisted on his presence in Paris to receive the shipment.<ref name=sisgov/>

==Assassination==
{{See also|Operation Opera#Strategy and diplomacy}}
On 14 June 1980, El Mashad was found dead in his room at the [[Le Méridien]] hotel in Paris.{{Sfn|Bar-Joseph|Handel|Perlmutter|2003|p= xxxvii}}  Some sources state that he was found with his throat cut and multiple stab wounds, others that he had been bludgeoned to death.<ref>{{cite news|last=Samuels|first=David|title=Q&A: Tzipi Livni The Kadima leader says Israel is not the safest place in the world for Jews| url=http://www.tabletmag.com/news-and-politics/46846/qa-tzipi-livni/|access-date=23 August 2011|work=Tablet Magazine|date=8 October 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last1=Weissman|first1=Stephen 'Steve'|title=The Islamic bomb: the nuclear threat to Israel and the Middle East|year=1981|publisher=Times Books|location=New York, NY|isbn=978-0-8129-0978-4|page=[https://archive.org/details/islamicbombnu00weis/page/275 275]|last2=Krosney|first2=Herbert|url=https://archive.org/details/islamicbombnu00weis/page/275}}.</ref>{{Sfn|Bar-Joseph|Handel|Perlmutter|2003|p=56}} Weeks later, a Parisian sex worker, alleged to have a connection to Mashad's death, was killed by a [[Hit and run|hit-and-run]] automobile.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2012/01/the-long-tradition-of-killing-middle-eastern-nuclear-scientists/251338/|title=The Long Tradition of Killing Middle Eastern Nuclear Scientists|first=Don|last=Peck|date=12 January 2012|website=The Atlantic}}</ref>
French authorities suspected the [[Israel|Israeli]] intelligence agency Mossad, but had no proof.<ref>{{cite book|last=Grossman|first=Mark|title=Encyclopedia of the Persian Gulf War|year=1995|publisher=ABC-CLIO| location=Santa Barbara|isbn=978-0-87436-684-6|page=218}}</ref> Israel issued statements immediately after El Mashad's death, claiming that the Iraqi nuclear program had been set back, but denied involvement.<ref name = styan>Styan, David. ''France and Iraq: Oil, Arms and French Policy Making in the Middle East''. I.B. Tauris, 2006. p. 134.</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Moore|first=Dan McKinnon|title=Bullseye one|year=1988|publisher=Berkley|location=New York|isbn=978-0-425-11259-5|edition=[Rev.]Berkley|page=[https://archive.org/details/bullseyeiraq00mcki/page/82 82]|url=https://archive.org/details/bullseyeiraq00mcki/page/82}}</ref>
